title: Why Is the Ocean Salty?
description: Rivers are fresh water, so where does all the ocean's salt come from? #science #ocean #shorts

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pip, why is the ocean salty? Did somebody spill the world's biggest bag of chips?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, Dunk. The salt comes from rocks on land.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rocks? I lick rocks all the time and they taste like dirt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Please stop doing that. Rain is slightly acidic, so it slowly breaks rocks down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That releases tiny amounts of minerals, and rivers carry them to the sea.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But rivers aren't salty. I've checked. With my mouth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, there's only a little in each river. The trick is evaporation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The sun lifts pure water out of the ocean, but the salt stays behind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do that for millions of years and the salt really piles up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the ocean is basically a giant pot of soup that never stops boiling.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sort of. Vents on the seafloor add minerals too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So: rocks give the salt, rivers deliver it, and evaporation traps it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cool. I'm still blaming the chips.
